Between January and August 2017, a total of
3183 patients were randomly assigned to oral
semaglutide (1591 patients) or placebo (1592 pa-
tients). The median time in the trial (including
follow-up) was 15.9 months (range, 0.4 to 20.0),
and approximately 75% of the patients received
oral semaglutide or placebo for more than 1 year.
In total, 3172 patients (99.7%) completed the
trial; 1347 (84.7%) completed the trial regimen
with oral semaglutide and 1435 (90.1%) with
placebo (Fig. S2 in the Supplementary Appen-
dix). Vital-status information was collected for
the 11 patients who did not complete the trial,
thus accounting for all patients who took part.

Figure S2. Patient Disposition. Screened N=3418; screening failures N=235; randomized (FAS) N=3183. Oral semaglutide N=1591 (100%): did not complete trial N=5 (0.3%), withdrawals N=3 (0.2%), lost to follow-up N=2 (0.1%), vital status: alive N=4 (0.3%), dead N=1 (0.1%), unknown N=0; completed trial N=1586 (99.7%); completed treatment N=1347 (84.7%). Placebo N=1592 (100%): did not complete trial N=6 (0.4%), withdrawals N=1 (0.1%), lost to follow-up N=5 (0.3%), vital status: alive N=5 (0.3%), dead N=1 (0.1%), unknown N=0; completed trial N=1586 (99.6%); completed treatment N=1435 (90.1%). Did not complete treatment: semaglutide N=244 (15.3%), adverse event N=185 (11.6%), lack of effect N=4 (0.3%), lost to follow-up N=2 (0.1%), other N=53 (3.3%); placebo N=156 (9.8%), adverse event N=104 (6.5%), lack of effect N=5 (0.3%), lost to follow-up N=2 (0.1%), other N=45 (2.8%). Footnote: for patients not completing treatment, cause was investigator-considered primary reason. Final vital status obtained for all. FAS, full analysis set.

the primary outcome (time from randomization to first major cardiovascular event)
encompassed events occurring between randomization and the final follow-up visit. Because
the time of randomization varied between patients, the final follow-up visits were aligned at 5
weeks after the last trial-wide trial product dose (with the exception of patients who withdrew
from the trial). A stratified Cox proportional hazards model was used for the primary analysis,
with treatment group as a fixed factor, and stratification based on evidence of cardiovascular
disease/advanced chronic kidney disease at screening. Patients who did not have a primary
outcome event during the in-trial period were censored at the final follow-up visit, or at time
of withdrawal for patients who withdrew from the trial.
Testing was hierarchical: following confirmation of non-inferiority, a test for superiority versus
placebo was performed, thereby preserving the type 1 error in the strong sense at 5% (two-
sided). All primary and secondary analyses were performed on the full analysis set, including
all randomized patients.

counterevidence.implication: The primary time-to-event analysis censors participants without an event at final follow-up or at withdrawal, and the flow diagram records 2 vs 5 lost to follow-up. These establish that at least some participants could have incomplete follow-up; hence the judgment is probable rather than an unqualified yes. Even a conservative count of all trial noncompleters remains very small relative to the 137 events.

answers.justification: For the approved randomized time-to-first-MACE result, 3,183 randomized participants were analyzed as the full analysis set (1,591 vs 1,592). The article reports 3,172 completing the trial (99.7%), and vital status was obtained for all 11 who did not; the flow diagram further shows no unknown vital status and only 2 vs 5 lost to follow-up. Although these figures do not establish complete nonfatal MACE ascertainment through the full window for every participant, even treating all 11 trial noncompleters as unavailable would leave only about 0.3% potentially missing, far fewer than 137 observed primary events. Under the official near-all criterion, this supports probably yes rather than asserting every outcome record was observed.

unknowns: The exact number with MACE outcome ascertainment unavailable at the outcome-specific censoring time is not explicitly reported; trial completion and vital-status completeness do not prove complete nonfatal MI/stroke ascertainment after withdrawal or loss to follow-up.

The original registry bytes are unavailable and have not been substituted; they could contain additional prespecified detail, but the inspected article and supplement provide participant-flow and analysis-window information.
